content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after recent spikes; apply downward bias correction for first 5–7 days.
- After a price spike, model tends to overshoot and fail to correct quickly; reduce forecast slope by 10–15% in subsequent days.
- When sentiment history is flat (all 0.00), model exhibits strong mean-reversion bias; adjust forecast to align with recent 7–14 day moving average.
- In absence of sentiment signals, model overreacts to short-term volatility; dampen forecast volatility by smoothing with 3–5 day exponential decay.
- If true outcome shows sharp downward trend after a peak, model fails to recognize it; add early warning lag correction: reduce forecast by 2–3% per day for 3–5 days post-peak.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-stage mean reversion; adjust final 5–7 days to match 14-day moving average of true values.
